_comment: Everything about YOUR channel lives here. Change values in this file rather than editing code - every script reads from it.

channel._handle_comment: Placeholder - set to the real handle once the channel exists.
channel.angle: I tell the true stories written into the planet - the eruptions, earthquakes, impacts, ice ages and slow collisions that built the world and will reshape it again - using the evidence scientists actually dug up: USGS, NASA and NOAA records, rock layers, ice cores and real footage.

video._comment: YouTube unlocks mid-roll ads at 8:00. 10-12 min is the sweet spot.
video._letterbox_comment: true adds 2.39:1 cinema bars over footage. Off by default: bars shrink the picture on phones, where most views happen.

storyboard._comment: Shot planning, done after narration against the real word timings (pipeline/storyboard.py). All footage is planned as stock, cut where the narration changes subject; the stock stage fills a shot with as many short clips as it needs and only shots no library can show become AI. Cards are documentary question/fact cards and numbers are big key-figure shots - both capped, never captions.

charts3d._comment: GPT-6 Astra (OPENAI_API_KEY) writes a bespoke three.js/Remotion component for every chart shot, designed for that data and line of narration. Each must pass static rules, tsc, a full test render and a vision read-back of its numbers, or it falls back to the built-in chart (pipeline/charts3d.py). Big-number shots always use the built-in component. Prices per million tokens, re-checked 20 Sep 2026 and unchanged; reasoning tokens bill as output. Cached input bills at 90% off, and a prompt over 272K tokens bills at 2x input / 1.5x output for the whole request - neither applies at this repo's prompt sizes.

visuals._comment: AI visuals via fal.ai (FAL_KEY) - the LAST resort on this channel, for scenes no camera recorded (deep-time landscapes) and shots no library could fill. Real footage from NASA, Wikimedia Commons, Pexels and Pixabay comes first (pipeline/stock.py). Every AI shot gets a keyframe image; the highest-priority ones are animated until the estimate hits budget_usd, the rest get depth-parallax camera moves. Cached by content hash in runs/<id>/assets/gen/.
visuals._prices_comment: Re-checked 20 Sep 2026, all still current. These figures drive the budget ledger, not the bill - fal charges what it charges, and these only decide how many shots get animated before the cap stops it. So where a price is uncertain, the SAFE direction is to overestimate. Three notes: (1) nano-banana-2 is $0.08 base but pipeline/fal.py asks for 2K, which bills at 1.5x - hence $0.12. Change both together. (2) h3-max 768P is $0.04/sec on a launch promotion until 30 Sep 2026, then $0.08. It is left at $0.08 deliberately: until the promo ends the ledger overestimates by 2x and animates fewer clips than the $5 cap really allows, which is the right way round to be wrong. (3) depth-anything v2 could not be re-verified on 20 Sep - $0.005 is carried over from 14 Sep and is the smallest line here either way.

models._comment: Model IDs change. If a call 404s, check the provider's docs and update here - no code change needed.

writer._comment: Renamed Sept 2026: 'deepseek-v4-flash' became 'deepseek-flash' (V4.1 Flash) on 10 Sep. 'deepseek-v4-pro' reroutes to V4.1 Flash from 04:00 UTC on 14 Sep, so polish_model points there too until V4.1 Pro ships - then change polish_model back to it.

writer_fallback._comment: gemini-3.1-flash was retired; renamed to gemini-3.5-flash. Moved to gemini-3.8-flash on 15 Sep 2026: newer, and $0.75/$3.75 per 1M tokens vs 3.5 Flash's $1.50/$9.00. Re-checked 20 Sep 2026: still $0.75/$3.75, introductory until 31 Dec 2026, then both rates double to $1.50/$7.50 on 1 Jan 2027. This is the FALLBACK writer, so it only bills when DeepSeek is down - but diarise that date, because it is a silent 2x on the day it lands.

tts._comment: ElevenLabs eleven_multilingual_v2, one fixed voice and seed (the Boring Docs channel proved Gemini TTS re-rolls the voice between chunks). VOICE NOT CHOSEN YET: pick one by ear at elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library - deliberately NOT Bren, which narrates The Boring Docs - and paste its id into elevenlabs_voice_id. Avoid voices with a custom-rate credit multiplier. Voice pace changes runtime by ~15%.
tts._style_comment: Prepended to every narration chunk as a spoken-style instruction (Gemini TTS follows it and does not read it aloud - verified 14 Sep 2026). Empty string for the voice's natural read (the default - a British RP style was tried 14 Sep 2026 and the natural read was preferred).

thumbnail._comment: Three concepts from the polish pass (or generated here for older runs) -> one image each with image_model -> Pillow draws the text and symbol -> a vision model runs the shrink test and ranks them. thumbnail.jpg is the winner; _b and _c are for YouTube Studio's Test & Compare.

safety._comment: review_only=true means nothing goes public on its own. The finished video is still uploaded to YouTube - that is how you review it on your phone - but at upload_privacy, and only your 'publish' reply makes it public. upload_privacy is the state it sits in while you review: 'private' (only your account) or 'unlisted' (anyone with the link, easier to open on a second device). Flip review_only to false after your Phase 1 numbers say the format works.
